title.en: Language work for Harvest Hymn: farm tools, new words, silent letters, a talk and a slogan

text.en: A harvest hymn thanks the earth and the farmer. The language work gives us the names of farm tools, words from older English, silent letters that we write but do not say, a way to give a group talk and a way to write a short slogan.

text.en:
Farm tools have special names, and each name tells the job. A rake has a long handle with metal teeth and collects hay or leaves. A trowel is a small hand tool for digging and making shallow furrows.
A sickle is a hand tool with a curved blade and a short handle, and it is used to harvest crops. A scythe has a long curved blade on a long handle and cuts tall grass. A plough is pulled by oxen and turns over the soil so that seeds can be sown. A spade has a flat rectangular blade on a long wooden handle and is used to dig the soil.
When a word is new, we can guess its meaning from the words around it, called context clues. In 'The king was beneficent to the poor because he took good care of them', the reason after because shows that beneficent means kind.
Munificent means very generous, as in a person who donates a lot to the needy. Succour means help given in trouble, as in friends supporting someone who has lost a job.
Radiance means brightness, as when the sun's rays fill a dark room. Ineffable means too great to be described in words, as in the ineffable joy of a child with a gift.
Archaic words are old words that were once common but are now used mostly in poems and old books. Morrow means tomorrow, hither means to this place, quoth means said, betwixt means between, and yonder means over there.
In English some letters are written but not pronounced, and these are called silent letters. In knife, know and knowledge, the k is silent.
The letter n is silent when it comes after m at the end of a word, as in hymn, column, autumn and solemn. The letter b is silent when it comes after m, as in womb, tomb, bomb, climb and comb. Say these words aloud and notice that the last letter makes no sound.
For the listening task you hear a talk on paddy cultivation. Listen for the steps and number them in order, then listen again to answer questions on the main step of preparing the soil, how long seeds take to grow into seedlings and why grains are dried after threshing.
Steps in growing rice include ploughing, puddling, transplanting seedlings, irrigating, harvesting, threshing and milling. Puddling means working the wet soil into a soft mud before planting seedlings. Confirm the exact order from the talk when you listen.
For the speaking task, work in a group and present a popular harvest dish of your region. Cover its name and other names, its ingredients, how it is cooked and served, its taste, any special ritual and a memory linked to it, and let every member speak.
A good presentation has a clear order. Greet the audience, introduce your group and topic, explain the structure, speak about each point with linking phrases such as Let us begin by, Next, and I would now like to discuss, then conclude with To summarise and thank the audience.
A slogan is a short, catchy sentence that spreads a message. It focuses on one main idea, uses simple language and is brief. Examples are 'Learn, Grow, Succeed' and 'Go Green by Keeping the Planet Clean'.
To write a slogan for the school notice board to thank farmers, choose the main idea, which is gratitude for food, and say it in a few words, for example 'Thank a farmer, thank your plate'. Then write it on chart paper and decorate it.
Sample slogan checks: Is it short? Is the message clear? Is the language simple? Does it catch attention with rhythm or a play on words? If yes to all four, the slogan is ready.

problem.en: Match each tool with its job and say why the harvest word 'sickle' is used for crops but 'scythe' for grass. Then name the silent letter in 'climb'.

text.en: A sickle has a short handle and a curved blade for cutting crops, and a scythe has a long handle and a long curved blade for tall grass.

why.en: The handle and blade decide the job.

text.en: In 'climb', the letter b is silent because it follows m.
Both tools cut, but the length of the blade and handle shows the kind of plant.

prompt.en: Say what an archaic word is, give two examples with their present-day meanings, and give one rule for silent letters.

requiredIdeas.en: old words now used mostly in poems and old books
morrow means tomorrow and hither means to this place
the n after m at the end is silent, as in hymn, or the b after m is silent, as in comb

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking archaic words are made-up words

points.en: Rake, trowel, sickle, scythe, plough and spade are farm tools with different jobs.
Context clues help us guess a word's meaning.
Archaic words: morrow, hither, quoth, betwixt, yonder.
Silent n after m (hymn) and silent b after m (comb).
A slogan is short, simple and gives one clear message.
